2019-02-12.summary: Four hours through Yanaka and Ueno to Akihabara, enjoying the quiet streets despite doubts about the photographs.

paragraphs: I walked for at least four hours from Nishi-Niporri all the way to Akihabara, going through Yanaka and Ueno. I have not seen photos yet, but I do not have high hopes. Very few people were roaming those streets to take photos of. Yet, I enjoyed walks a lot; It was calm and relaxing.

2019-02-18.summary: A half-day of experimenting with harsh light and contrast.

paragraphs: Spent half a day walking with a camera. Not sure if I got any good pictures, but I did experiment with harsh light and contrast. Curious to see if it worked or not.
Night photography will not happen today, 4 hours or walk is a bit too much. I might return to Shinjuku in day or two to try night photography.

2019-02-22.summary: Photographing Friday-night streets around Kita-Senju station on digital.

paragraphs: Now I’m walking nearby Kita-Senju station taking photos of people enjoying Friday night. In back of my mind I know that I take pictures of things and streets, no people—I do not have enough confidence yet. I’m shooting digital today. I do not have high speed film for night streets.

2019-03-08.summary: A day among Nikko’s temples, parks and the Imperial Villa, ending in a coffee shop.

paragraphs: Sweet, sweet day walking around Nikko. Temples, parks, hikes and very cool Imperial Villa. Now sitting in a very cite coffee shop about to leave to Tokyo.

2019-03-18.summary: A photo walk from Harajuku to Ginza with art galleries along the way.

paragraphs: I somehow managed to walk from Harajuku to Ginza by feet. Tokyo suddenly seems tad smaller. All fo this was part of the photowalk with couple of art galleries in between. Overall, good day.

I have problem with my photos though. I don’t like anything I shoot. It’s not like I’m bored with photography. Quite the opposite, I’m itching to go out and shoot, but I’m bored with a type of photos I make. Something has to click, and I’m looking for it.

2020-11-22.summary: Slow walking, time to think, and photographs made with a Leica Q2.

paragraphs: I had slow but very long walks. Under 10 clicks in about five hours. Which is 2kph or so. Slow, but pleasant. Time to think, clean mind, and take pictures.

Every time I take my Leica Q2, I’m doubting myself whether I should’ve got one in the first place. Shooting experience is similar to modern digital camera, which I don’t really enjoy that much. Although, when I review files—I like most of them.

2022-10-01.summary: The third scheduled Osanpo heads toward Mizumoto Park, exploring unfamiliar parts of Katsushika.

paragraphs: Today was third Osanpo (お散歩) since I started to schedule those a month or so ago. I took train to Ochanomizu and headed to Mizumoto Park. It is not a momiji season yet, but I was curious to see the park and akso it was in a direction I never walked.

That part of Tokyo is quite interesting. Main streets have very near-looking corners and cozy aura around them. Residential areas are also extremely warm and scenic (but not in an European way). There are bits of the city, specially further north—that looks completly like suburbs: very wide streets, big houses, quite low density of everything.
Katsushika is one of those wards I have never visited before. It looks like Adachi, but not a Kita-Senju.

2022-10-22.summary: From Tokyo station toward Disneyland via Sunamachi Ginza, reflecting on the direction of long-walk photography.

paragraphs: Another long walk (Osanpo, お散歩) in the books! I started at Tokyo station and went all the way to the edge of the city to the Disneyland.

Along the way I managed to see Sunamachi Ginza once again. It was a nice 16km walk, but my photography was not the sharpest. I feel like I’m slowly getting over of long-walk photography and have to pivot in a different direction, I just do not know where.

Quite happy with a walk I hope didn’t fuck up the metering on all of the shots. I know at least three frames are bad.

2024-07-18.summary: Following Rome’s Aurelian Walls without a map and photographing what stands in front of them.

paragraphs: I had fairly short, but very hot, walk around Aurelian Walls around Rome.
Somehow I ended up at Colosseum after walking up the street next to east gate — Porta Metronia. I didn’t use maps for walking as I was following the wall.

Somewhere I in first roll of this three-roll walk I started to shoot things in front of the Aurelian Walls — some shots don’t have wall at all. Although there was a bit of where what was in front of the wall — were other walls — mostly of expensive villas or private land. Some wall with torn cloth (?) were a funny contrast to the actual AWs.

2024-07-23.summary: A west-wall walk after discovering how little of the northern wall remains, finishing near Ponte Sisto.

paragraphs: I was supposed to take a long walk around the northern part of the Aurelian Walls, but surprise, surprise, only 200-400 meters of it remain near Roma Termini.
I walked the whole part from Alsmots St. Peter (from Gianicolo Museum) to the Tiber and then some more along the shore.
Two and a half rolls later, I ended up at Ponte Sisto.

2025-12-13.summary: A walk toward Ikebukuro, discovering new streets, small neighborhoods and a possibly abandoned Rolls-Royce.

paragraphs: Leica cameras have this magic that pulls you in. I love it. I went for a medium-distance walk from my home to Ikebukuro, which felt like about three to three and a half hours.

That was quite good. Somehow, I ended up on some streets I had already been to, but most of them were new. I found a few cute places, perhaps found an old abandoned Rolls-Royce somewhere in the northern part, and also a few cute neighborhoods.
It was a good reminder of how nice walking is and how pleasant it usually is.
